reason: The cited evidence discusses limited atomic mobility and disorder-to-order transitions in HEA nanoparticles, but none provides direct support for localized nanoscale melting, transient liquid domains, or heating-rate effects on phase transitions. The key premises about melting-point depression and liquid-mediated re-arrangement are not backed by the cited passages.
premises: High surface-to-volume ratio in nanoparticles lowers the local melting point
Limited atomic mobility in the solid delays re-ordering until local melting occurs
Transient nanoscale liquid domains mediate atomic re-arrangement and phase transition
Heating rate influences the onset/extent of phase transition via temperature homogenization
Phase transition occurs below the bulk melting point due to localized melting
